glossary.definition: A GPU is a chip originally built for rendering video game graphics that turns out to also be extremely good at the kind of repetitive, parallel math AI training needs. A regular computer processor is like one extremely skilled worker doing tasks one at a time very quickly; a GPU is like thousands of less specialized workers all doing simple tasks simultaneously, which happens to be exactly the kind of work training a neural network requires. Access to GPUs, and the electricity to run them, is one of the biggest bottlenecks and cost centers in AI right now.

items.title: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage
items.summary: The company is said to be significantly dropping the amount it's spending on AI for its engineering teams. Apple is cutting the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. It’s a big change for a company that has worked to integrate the technology into its engineering processes. In October, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for its engineering teams, decreasing it from $300 to $200, the outlet reported.

items.title: The Blue Wave Has Tech Bros Scrambling for Data Centers in Space
items.summary: After Democrats won big in Texas and other AI infrastructure hot spots on Tuesday, data center enthusiasts looked for comfort in low Earth orbit. A wave of Democratic candidates across the country —and notably in Texas, a national data center hotspot and home to Elon Musk’s SpaceX—won their state and congressional races on Tuesday, including many candidates who voiced opposition to the data center industry . The results have sent some corners of the tech industry looking to the heavens for answers. In recent hours, data center enthusiasts have proclaimed on social media that they’re still “ bullish ” on building data centers—just not necessarily in Texas, or even on Earth at all.

items.title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
items.summary: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges.

items.title: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared
items.summary: AI industry PACs spent millions influencing the 2026 midterms, with mixed results. Political groups are already looking toward the next election cycle. Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races.

items.title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
items.summary: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.

items.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor, whose app runs several coding agents at once
items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. has acquired artificial intelligence coding startup Conductor in a deal first reported today by Axios. Conductor confirmed it’s joining Meta in a post on its website. Terms were not disclosed. The company’s software lets a developer run several coding agents at once, each in an isolated copy of the codebase, and then review and merge what they produce.

items.title: What AI's growing share of tech spending means for enterprises in 2027
items.summary: AI spending is reshaping enterprise IT budgets. How CIOs can manage rising costs, prioritize investments and measure returns beyond productivity gains.

items.title: ChatGPT can now turn text prompts and photos into animated GIFs with OpenAI's Images 2.6 model
items.summary: OpenAI is adding a GIF feature to ChatGPT. With the new Images 2.6 model, users can create animated GIFs from text prompts or photos and then adjust speed and individual frames. The model's image consistency is strong enough to keep characters recognizable across frames, making flipbook-style animation possible. According to OpenAI, users now generate more than four billion images per week.

items.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
items.summary: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott.

items.title: OpenAI's Codex Helps in Aerodynamic Engineering for Mazda
items.summary: OpenAI’s forward-deployed engineers are working with Mazda's aerodynamics and crash-safety engineers to explore how its AI models can help develop and evaluate vehicle designs. The research collaboration will use airflow and structural behaviour simulations to assess vehicle performance while accounting for styling and manufacturing costs. OpenAI is working with the Japanese car maker on aerodynamic design. GPT-6 Astra, used through Codex, helps Mazda engineers explore different vehicle nose shapes, simulate airflow and identify designs that could reduce aerodynamic drag.

items.title: MariaDB enhances agent development for its next-gen database platform
items.summary: MariaDB on Wednesday said it was adding four new agent-focused capabilities to Enterprise Platform 2027, the latest version of its enterprise database platform, to help developers retrieve enterprise data faster, maintain agent memory across sessions, and reduce the cost and latency of repeated model queries. These new capabilities include AI Retrieval, AI Plugins, Agent Memory, and Semantic Cache. While AI Retrieval is designed to help agents access information from enterprise documents and live operational data through a single managed service, AI Plugins are designed to bring MariaDB-specific expertise into coding agents such as Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex , helping developers generate database-related code more accurately, the company said in a statement. AI Retrieval also converts natural-language questions into read-only SQL queries, which MariaDB said would eliminate the need for developers to manually write queries for every request.

items.title: Tech layoffs: A 2026 timeline
items.summary: Among a range of factors leading to a wave of tech sector layoffs in 2026 is the rapid rise of artificial intelligence and automation. Companies are reconfiguring their workforces to leverage AI for increased efficiency and reduced operating costs. This realignment and reduction is implemented even by companies reporting strong financial performance. But it’s not just AI leading to workforce cuts.
